name: ddc
description: A synthesizable, parameterizable Digital Down Converter (DDC) that mixes a real bandpass input to complex baseband with an NCO, decimates with a multiplierless CIC, and flattens droop with a compensation FIR, producing a decimated complex I/Q stream.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Synthesizable, parameterizable Digital Down Converter. The top ddc takes a real bandpass input stream (Q1.15) and mixes a selected band down to complex baseband using a numerically controlled oscillator (NCO): a PAW-bit phase accumulator advances by a runtime tuning word ftw and the top AW phase bits address an NSIN-entry sine ROM, with cosine reusing the same ROM via a quarter-table index offset. A signed mixer forms I = x*cos and Q = x*(-sin), round-half-up and saturated to Q1.15. Each lane is decimated by R with a multiplierless Hogenauer CIC (STAGES integrators at the input rate, decimation, then STAGES combs at the output rate), and a per-lane direct-form compensation FIR removes the CIC sin(x)/x droop. The interface is valid-only: in_valid strobes every input sample and out_valid pulses once per R inputs; there is no ready/backpressure handshake.
key_decisions: The NCO sine ROM is generated by genddc.py as a deterministic combinational case-ROM (rtl/ddc_nco.v); it deliberately maps to LUTs not BRAM because the target BRAM is init-none and the flow runs with --ignore-initial.
Fixed-point is Q1.15 throughout (DW/OUTW/IQW/SW/CW = 16), with mixer and FIR results round-half-up and symmetrically saturated.

CIC defaults are STAGES=4, R=8, M=1; internal registers are sized IQW + Bmax where Bmax = ceil(N*log2(R*M)) = 12 bits, and the comb output is arithmetically right-shifted by Bmax to renormalize the (R*M)^N DC gain.
Cosine reuses the single sine ROM by adding a quarter table (NSIN/4) to the index, the same twiddle-ROM trick used by blocks/fft.

Replicated hardware is modeled with generate: the CIC is built as generate chains (one register+adder per stage) and the FIR instantiates one multiplier per tap into a products array followed by an explicit running-sum reduction, avoiding procedural unrolled MAC loops; no functions in RTL.

FIR coefficients are packed into a single [NTAP*CW-1:0] parameter H (Q1.15, tap i at H[i*CW +: CW]); the default is a unit impulse at the center tap and the CIC+FIR pair is instantiated per lane (I and Q) via a generate loop.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; the NCO sine table is generated by the generator script. Follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: E. B. Hogenauer, 'An economical class of digital filters for decimation and interpolation,' IEEE Trans. Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing, vol. 29, no. 2, pp. 155-162, 1981.
R. E. Crochiere and L. R. Rabiner, Multirate Digital Signal Processing, Prentice-Hall, 1983.
J. Tierney, C. M. Rader, and B. Gold, 'A digital frequency synthesizer,' IEEE Trans. Audio and Electroacoustics, vol. 19, no. 1, pp. 48-57, 1971.
U. Meyer-Baese, Digital Signal Processing with Field Programmable Gate Arrays, Springer.
R. G. Lyons, Understanding Digital Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Prentice Hall, 2010, ch. 13 (CIC filters) and ch. 13.32 (DDC structure).
